newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end off for second day on gains-taking.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end off for second day on gains-taking.

text.p: Brazil shares closed off for a second consecutive day on profit-taking as investors scooped up gains from a spectacular first half of the year.
The Bovespa index of the 48 most traded stocks closed off 0.9 percent at 12,758 points. Market turnover remained high at 1.295 billion reais or $1.2 billion.

Traders said domestic funds, which bought heavily early in the week, were cutting their purchases as the quarter draws to a close. "It is natural that they would take a break at some point," said a senior trader. The funds have been the driving force behind the bolsa's 80 percent rise so far in 1997.
Analysts said the bolsa could suffer more profit-taking Monday, the last day of the first half, and resume its uptrend in the following sessions.
But the rise should be moderate as investors stay guarded ahead of next week's U.S. Federal Reserve meeting, although U.S. interest rates are widely expected to remain steady.
Although the Fed meeting will hold the market's attention, the influx of cash is the factor which will continue dictating the bolsa's rise, analysts said.
"Now what everybody wants to know is how much money is coming into stock funds," another trader said.
Bellweather Telebras preferred fell 0.42 percent at 166.80 reais, while state oil firm Petrobras preferred lost 2.58 percent to close at 302 reais.
Federal power holding Eletrobras preferred dropped 1.67 percent, ending at 649 reais. The decline contributed to a 2.15 percent drop in the Sao Paulo's power sector index .IEE to 3,351 points.
The index comprises the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector.
While most blue chips posted losses, some second-tier stocks resisted the profit-taking.
The voting stock of Banco Itau surged 5.43 percent to close at 485 reais following the bank's acquisition of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj.

Itau's purchase of Banerj took the bank's total assets to about 37.7 billion reais, according to Itau's estimates based on its first quarter results. The bank is now just 1.5 billion reais behind Bradesco, the country's top private bank with some 39 billion reais in assets.
Bradesco common, in turn, fell 0.18 percent to 10.98 reais. Itau bought Banerj for 311.1 million reais, but it will pay for the bank with privatization bonds purchased at a 50 percent discount.
